name: Snow Jasmine
description: Golden jasmine tea from Yuanjiang Valley, with a floral aroma, grape-like sweetness and gentle acidity.
blend: 92% cold-brewed jasmine tea; grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: A light lunch, a fruit dessert, or the first glass of an unhurried evening.
photoAlt: A glass of Chalu at the table
pairings: Steamed fish with ginger
A gentle, aromatic dish that leaves room for the jasmine to shine.
Fresh prawn rice-paper rolls
Fresh herbs and a light filling meet the tea’s delicate floral character.
Pear & almond tart
A softly fruity finish alongside the tea’s gentle sweetness.

name: Hibiscus Noir
description: A caffeine-free hibiscus and camellia blend. Red-fruit aromas meet floral notes and a structured finish.
blend: 94% cold-brewed herbal tea (hibiscus, wild camellia, strawberry, raspberry); grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: A cheese board, good conversation, and an evening that stretches a little longer.
photoAlt: Chalu Hibiscus Noir served with food
pairings: Roast duck
Berry aromas and a structured finish make a lively partner for a richer plate.
Mushroom risotto
An earthy, savoury dish with a contrasting lift of red-fruit character.
A soft cheese board
Creamy textures meet fragrant berry notes—an easy pairing to share.

name: Volcano Oolong
description: Tengchong oolong, toasted and rested on Yunnan oak. Dry, nutty and mineral in character.
blend: 94% cold-brewed oolong tea; grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: Bring it to a seafood supper, or take your time with a glass all on its own.
photoAlt: Chalu poured into a glass for serving
pairings: Grilled sea bass
A little char echoes the tea’s toasted character without overpowering the fish.
Roast chicken with herbs
Savoury, golden flavours sit naturally alongside the oolong’s nutty depth.
Roasted mushrooms
Earthy flavours make room for the tea’s warm oak and mineral character.

name: Untamed Rosé
description: White Pu’er, rose, berries, citrus and pepper. A dry rosé expression with a lively finish.
blend: The featured blend brings together white Pu’er, rose petals, berries, citrus and Yunnan black pepper. This is a blend overview; consult the bottle label for the complete ingredient declaration.
pairing: An open-air lunch, a fruit dessert, or a just-because toast with friends.
pairings: Salmon with lemon
Citrus notes bring a bright counterpoint to the richness of the fish.
Burrata & tomato salad
Fresh acidity and creamy cheese meet a dry, berry-led pour.
Strawberry tart
A fruit-forward match that echoes the tea’s summer-berry aromas.
